The BLM’s rule defines an e-bike as a bicycle with a small electric motor of not more than 750 watts (one horsepower) which assists in the operation of the bicycle and reduces the physical exertion demands on the rider. E-bikes may have two or three wheels and must have fully operable pedals. Some e-bikes only provide motorized assistance when the rider is pedaling; others can operate without pedaling. Some e-bikes cease to provide motorized assistance to the rider when the bicycle reaches the speed of 20 miles per hour (mph). Others cease to provide motorized assistance when the bicycle reaches 28 mph E-bikes may appear virtually indistinguishable from traditional bicycles. What is the difference between the classes of e-bikes? Class 1 e-bikes are equipped with a motor that provides assistance only when the rider is pedaling, and that ceases to provide assistance when the bicycle reaches the speed of 20 mph. E-bikes help make public lands more accessible to more people. An e-bike is a bicycle with a small electric motor of not more than 750 watts (one horsepower) which assists in the operation of the bicycle and reduces the physical exertion demands on the rider. E-bikes may have two or three wheels and must have fully operable pedals. Where can I ride my E-bike? BLM-managed public lands offer many opportunities for riding e-bikes, including motorized areas and OHV trails. Search for an Open OHV area or motorized trail to ride your e-bike. BLM offices also have the authority to identify which non-motorized trails could be used for e-bike use on BLM-managed lands. BLM District and Field Managers are encouraged to consider authorizing e-bike use in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, including the e-bike rule. Contact your local BLM office for more information. What is an electric bicycle, or e-bike? E-bikes are bicycles with fully operable pedals and a small electric motor that does not exceed 750 watts (one horsepower). The motor assists in the operation of the bicycle and reduces the rider’s physical exertion demands. There are different classes of e-bikes based on how it assists the rider and what speed the bike can reach. Different classes may be managed separately on public lands. For example, a trail may only be open to Class 1 e-bikes. For more information, please visit the e-bikes FAQ page . E. coli and Salmonella Outbreak Linked to Alfalfa Sprouts For Everyone Oct. 1, 2026 Food safety alert Investigation status: Open Recall issued: Yes CDC and public health officials in several states are investigating a multistate outbreak of E. coli and Salmonella infections linked to alfalfa sprouts. If you have recalled sprouts in your home, throw them out or return them to where you purchased them. Updates Locations Timeline Fast Facts Cases : 76 (21 new) Hospitalizations : 6 (2 new) Deaths : 0 States : 16 (1 new) Updates Locations Timeline Notice Urgent This outbreak involves two pathogens, Salmonella and E. coli , and three people have been infected with both. Earth Systems Modeling Earth system models simulate how chemistry, biology, and physical forces work together across our globe. Climate system models (which are part of Earth system models) describe how seasonal to climate variations and other extremes have behaved over multiple years and decades. All components of Earth’s systems, such as the atmosphere, oceans, sea and land ice, and land and ecosystems affect these variations. Scientists run various scenarios with these models. The scenarios show how different human and environmental activities might affect future energy systems and how these energy systems might in turn influence Earth’s future. This information is useful to a broad range of potential stakeholders and decision makers involved with understanding and planning for a healthy economy and the resiliency of our nation’s diverse communities. Politics Judge orders an inquiry into potential DOJ misconduct in Trump's golf course case October 30, 2026 5:56 PM ET By Rachel Treisman Workers remove downed trees from the East Potomac golf course on Monday. Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP hide caption toggle caption i Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP WASHINGTON, D.C. — A federal judge is launching a formal inquiry into potential misconduct by Trump administration officials in the lawsuit over East Potomac Park, including whether they repeatedly misrepresented the president's plans for the municipal D.C. golf course. District Judge Ana Reyes ordered Friday's hearing — the third in as many weeks — to seek clarity from government lawyers days after they acknowledged in writing Wednesday that there is a plan to transform the municipal golf course into a championship-level venue, closing it and much of the surrounding park in mid-November. For months, Justice Department attorneys representing the Interior Department and National Park Service had maintained in court filings and hearings that such a plan was not yet final, despite President Trump's social media statements proclaiming otherwise. For decades, weight loss has been framed as eating less—but research suggests the problem isn’t food itself, it’s how calories are packaged. Nathan Tia, Simplynate Photography/Getty Images By Hannah Singleton Published May 6, 2026 A few bites of a pastry can deliver as many calories as an entire plate of chicken, vegetables, and starch, while taking a fraction of the time to eat. That mismatch points to a blind spot in how weight loss has long been understood. In controlled feeding studies, diets higher in ultra-processed foods lead people to consume more calories overall, even when meals are designed to be nutritionally similar or smaller in volume. pages.text: Ebola global Skip to main content Overview Ebola disease is a severe, often fatal illness affecting humans and other primates. The virus is transmitted to people from wild animals (such as fruit bats, porcupines and non-human primates) and then spreads in the human population through direct contact with the blood, secretions, organs or other bodily fluids of infected people, and with surfaces and materials (e.g. bedding, clothing) contaminated with these fluids. The average Ebola disease case fatality rate is around 50%. Case fatality rates have varied from 25–90% in past outbreaks. The first Ebola disease outbreaks occurred in remote villages in Central Africa, near tropical rainforests. The 2014–2016 Ebola virus disease outbreak in West Africa was the largest and most complex Ebola outbreak since the virus was first discovered in 1976. There were more cases and deaths in this outbreak than all others combined. It also spread between countries, starting in Guinea then moving across land borders to Sierra Leone and Liberia. It is thought that fruit bats of the Pteropodidae family are natural hosts of the orthoebolavirus. Symptoms The incubation period, that is, the time interval from infection with the virus to onset of symptoms, is from 2 to 21 days. A person infected with Ebola cannot spread the disease until they develop symptoms. Symptoms of Ebola disease can be sudden and include: fever, fatigue, malaise, muscle, pain, headache, and sore throat. They regarded the specialised unit as a "death house" as not many patients do recover - especially those admitted in the late stages of the illness. His 50-year-old mother was in tears, pleading with him not to go there. "Why are you choosing to die at the Ebola treatment centre?" Masika Ndungo had asked him. But as a doctor at Butembo's Katwa Hospital, he knew that if stayed at home, he was unlikely to survive. The cricket boards of Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands are developing the concept and had hoped to play it as soon as the early part of next summer. pages.text: Eddie James: Wales' win against New Zealand the stuff of dreams - BBC Sport Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Image caption, Centre Eddie James made his Wales debut against South Africa in 2024 By Chris Kirwan BBC Sport Wales Published 15 November 2026 Eddie James conducted his post-match media duties at Principality Stadium while clutching a souvenir match ball. Perhaps the one he dotted down for one of Wales' five tries in the historic 35-28 win against New Zealand , maybe the one he wrapped up with his long right arm in one of many telling defensive moments. The 24-year-old Scarlets centre has become a firm fixture in Steve Tandy's starting line-up because of his strong running and offloading threat. He crossed down the left wing early in the second half, yet it is one of his 25 tackles that is one of the moments to watch and rewatch. At 35-21, a try looked certain when Anton Lienert-Brown burst towards the line but James reached out, stopped the New Zealand centre a metre out and ensured there was no offload. The All Blacks would go over one more time but it was a moment to encapsulate Wales' defensive desire. "I honestly can't feel a thing," he said while still in his kit, almost an hour after the final whistle. "I haven't been able feel my feet for a long time now. It was an amazing performance defensively. "We're such a small nation and we pride ourselves a lot on our heart." pages.text: Edmonia Lewis confronted American slavery in her sculptures. Then history forgot her. | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE Edmonia Lewis confronted American slavery in her sculptures. Then history forgot her. A new exhibition of her masterworks is traveling the country and reclaiming her place in American history. During her lifetime, Edmonia Lewis was America's most famous artists. Seen here, the biracial sculptor defied the odds and produced trailblazing work. Augustus Marshall, Courtesy Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture By Katy Kelleher Published June 15, 2026 Part celebrity, part anomaly, sculptor Edmonia Lewis captivated mid-19 th -century audiences with her luminous, large-scale marble sculptures that appeared nearly lifelike in their carefully rendered detail. For wealthy Americans on the Grand Tour, a stop at her studio was practically necessary. But visitors weren’t just there to follow in the footsteps of Pope Pius IX and President Ulysses S. Grant, both admirers of Lewis, they were there to obtain proof. They wanted to see with their own eyes that Lewis, a petite biracial woman, could render life from stone. For some, it beggared belief that her hands could have coaxed forth vivid expressions from blocks of Carrara marble. While she was able to delegate some of the brute work of carving to assistants, Lewis made a point of ensuring that the public saw her with a chisel in hand, an unusual choice for sculptors of the era. Even in the prime of her storied career, Lewis still needed to prove herself, to justify her talent

Not all fish, shellfish, or the insects that they eat can tolerate the same amount of acid. An ecosystem is a community of plants, animals and other organisms along with their environment including the air, water and soil. Everything in an ecosystem is connected. If something harms one part of an ecosystem – one species of plant or animal, the soil or the water – it can have an impact on everything else. Effects of Acid Rain on Fish and Wildlife The ecological effects of acid rain are most clearly seen in aquatic environments, such as streams, lakes, and marshes where it can be harmful to fish and other wildlife. As it flows through the soil, acidic rain water can leach aluminum from soil clay particles and then flow into streams and lakes. EFTPS 는 다음을 제공합니다: 신뢰할 수 있는 보안 안전한 인터넷 브라우저에서 납세자 식별 번호 ( EIN 또는 SSN ), 개인 식별 번호 ( PIN ) 및 인터넷 암호, 그리고 안전한 인터넷 브라우저를 병용하여 보안이 강화됩니다. 언제든 이용 가능한 편리성 납부일을 365일 까지 미리 예약할 수 있습니다. 집이나 사무실에서 언제든지 세금을 납부할 수 있습니다. 귀하의 소득, 고용, 연방세 중간예납 및 연방 특별 소비세를 납부할 수 있습니다. 예약된 세금 납부를 쉽게 변경하거나 취소할 수 있습니다. 이메일 알림으로 납부 상황을 추적할 수 있습니다. 지난 15개월 동안의 납부 내역을 확인할 수 있습니다. 고객 서비스 안내원으로부터 납부 또는 질문에 대한 도움을 받을 수 있습니다. 신뢰할 수 있는 정확성 귀하의 납부에 대한 즉각적 확인 내역과 귀하의 은행 명세서를 검토하여 납부 사실을 확인할 수 있습니다. 다수의 고객의 세금 납부를 할 수 있는 수용력 세무 전문가는, 단일 로그인으로 다수 고객의 세금을 납부할 수 있습니다. 무료 Batch Provider Software (일괄처리 제공자 소프트웨어)를 다운로드하십시오(영어) . 간행물 5301, 전자 연방 세금 납부 시스템 – 일괄처리 제공자 소프트웨어 사용자 매뉴얼(영어) PDF EFTPS 등록 방법 신규 EFTPS 등록은 업무일수로 최대 5일이 소요됩니다. In early 2017, the Department of Energy’s Office of Geothermal, formerly known as the Geothermal Technologies Office (GTO), funded national laboratories to focus on the office's vision for transformational enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) . The Office of Geothermal’s objective was to establish a collaborative experimental and model comparison initiative: the EGS Collab. The EGS Collab’s focus was to test and verify computational models that could be used in EGS work broadly or at the Office of Geothermal’s Frontier Observatory for Research in Geothermal Energy (FORGE) EGS field laboratory. The EGS Collab team comprised of eight national laboratories, six universities, and industrial partners. The EGS Collab was a small-scale field site where the subsurface modeling and research community conducted controlled, small-scale, in-situ experiments focused on rock fracture behavior and permeability enhancement. EGS Pilot Demonstrations The Office of Geothermal is supporting four enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) demonstration projects directed by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA). These projects will demonstrate EGS in a variety of geographic locations, geologic formations, and subsurface conditions. The results can help expand the use of firm, flexible geothermal energy to more locations nationwide. IIJA authorizes projects in four Topic Areas. pages.description: Fragments of a 4,500 year-old dress were stored in a museum’s basement for decades until one researcher pieced it back together, looking for answers about the mysterious relic.
pages.text: Egyptian Bead Dress | National Geographic HISTORY & CULTURE This Ancient Egyptian Fashion Enchanted a Pharaoh Fragments of a 4,500 year-old dress were stored in a museum’s basement for decades until one researcher pieced it back together, looking for answers about the mysterious relic. Millicent Jick's reconstructed net dress, of blue and green faience beads; broad collar with faience beads and gold pendants. 4th dynasty. Museum of Fine Arts, Boston SCALA, FLORENCE By Cathy Newman Published August 18, 2026 More than 4,500 years old, the Egyptian bead net dress at the Museum of Fine Arts (MFA), Boston, is the first complete example of its kind. The better part of a century after its discovery, it was meticulously reconstructed over a period of three years. The dress belonged to a female contemporary of Pharaoh Khufu (ca 2500 B.C.), builder of the Great Pyramid. The beads were found scattered over and around her mummified body, which had been lying inside a limestone sarcophagus in an undisturbed tomb beneath the famous Giza Plateau. As the sarcophagus was unmarked, the woman’s identity remains shrouded in mystery, but her burial on the Giza Plateau, the necropolis of kings, speaks to her prominence. Perhaps she was the wife of an upper-level bureaucrat, speculates Larry Berman, the MFA’s senior curator of Ancient Egyptian, Nubian, and Near Eastern art. In any case, she must certainly have been well connected to be buried there. A person’s residence, temporal or eternal— then as now— was a clear and unmistakable measure of status. Wednesday's opening hearing was adjourned until 18 November after defence lawyers representing the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr requested a new judge. The UN has warned of "widening assaults on press freedom by Egyptian authorities, including the targeting, persecution and harassment of independent journalists". Attalah told the BBC that a recent crackdown was meant to "send a chilling message" to "the very few newsrooms that are left". She warned: "Everybody should be careful, everybody should be scared, everybody should be wondering if they are next." Set up 13 years ago, Mada Masr became Egypt's leading independent news site with Attalah as its editor-in-chief and co-founder. Drumming, clashing cymbals, and shaking rattles, elite priestesses like the chantress Henettawy, shown here, and the newly unearthed chantress, Merit, played an important role in summoning the gods and securing blessings. Peter Horree, Alamy By Taylor Mitchell Brown Published August 25, 2026 The Beautiful Festival of the Valley was an annual celebration in ancient Egypt that connected the royal and wealthy dead with the gods. To initiate the splendid occasion, large crowds of priests gathered outside the temple of Karnak in Thebes. Then they collected statues of the ancient Egyptian deities associated with the temple: Amun, Mut, and Khonsu. Afterward, the revelers ferried the statues across the Nile to bless important tombs and temples. As part of the festivities, the divine effigies were enshrined within wooden sailing vessels called barques and bedecked with flowers, gold, and precious stones of turquoise, carnelian, and lapis lazuli.
